classification.difficultyReason: Use the calculated mean and standard deviation to form an interval, select its integer counts and sum three binomial probabilities.

content.prompt: It is known that 15% of a large constituency voted for the Working Together Party at the last election. A poll of 100 people is taken and they are asked whether they voted WTP.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the mean and standard deviation for this poll? Give the standard deviation correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: Mean: $15$ WTP voters; standard deviation: $\sqrt{12.75}\approx3.57$ WTP voters.
answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the number of WTP voters in the poll. Then $X\sim B(100,0.15)$.
$$\begin{aligned}\mu&=np=100(0.15)=15\\\sigma&=\sqrt{np(1-p)}=\sqrt{100(0.15)(0.85)}=\sqrt{12.75}\approx3.57\end{aligned}$$
The mean is 15 WTP voters and the standard deviation is approximately 3.57 WTP voters.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability that in the sample, the number of WTP voters lies within half a standard deviation of the mean? Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

answer.worked:
For $X\sim B(100,0.15)$, half a standard deviation gives the interval
$$15-\frac{\sqrt{12.75}}2\le X\le15+\frac{\sqrt{12.75}}2.$$
Its endpoints are approximately 13.215 and 16.785, so the possible integer values are 14, 15 and 16.
$$\begin{aligned}P(14\le X\le16)&=\sum_{x=14}^{16}\binom{100}{x}(0.15)^x(0.85)^{100-x}\\&\approx0.325\end{aligned}$$
